title: 1994 AHSME Problem 21
statement:
Find the number of counterexamples to the statement:

“If \(N\) is an odd positive integer the sum of whose digits is \(4\) and none of whose digits is \(0,\) then \(N\) is prime.”

solutions.text: The odd possibilities are \(13,31,121,211,\) and \(1111.\) The numbers \(13,31,\) and \(211\) are prime, while \(121=11^2\) and \(1111=11\cdot101.\) Thus there are \(2\) counterexamples. Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: A number satisfying the digit conditions has at most four digits
List the odd possibilities by composing \(4\) into positive digits
